name: ReaSCAN Syntax Generalization
summary: 16,378 commands to ground in grid worlds and translate into action sequences.
overview: ReaSCAN asks a model to identify an object described by an instruction and produce the actions to reach or move it in a grid world. The syntax conditions test longer conjunctions and nested relative clauses. [Original study, Sections 4 and 6.4](https://datasets-benchmarks-proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2021/file/2838023a778dfaecdc212708f721b788-Paper-round1.pdf)
methodology: The snapshot contains both complete Category C test sets from ReaSCAN v1.1. C1 has 8,375 examples with longer conjunctive clauses, and C2 has 8,003 examples with recursive relative clauses. Each prompt shows the original command words and a text rendering of the six-by-six grid, including the agent's starting position and facing and the placed objects. Each key combines the condition and the one-based row number. The revision is the SHA-256 of the C1 and C2 archive members concatenated in that order. [Release and data format](https://github.com/frankaging/Reason-SCAN/blob/1e6726aab70c915a3d3068bed77ae255feeaf6f1/README.md), [Original study, Table 3](https://datasets-benchmarks-proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2021/file/2838023a778dfaecdc212708f721b788-Paper-round1.pdf)
scoring: A prediction earns one point when its ordered action sequence exactly matches the release. The evaluator ignores letter case, separating whitespace, and a final period. Report accuracy separately for C1 and C2. [Original predictor](https://github.com/frankaging/Reason-SCAN/blob/1e6726aab70c915a3d3068bed77ae255feeaf6f1/code/models/seq2seq/predict.py#L37-L50)
limitations: The grid worlds and command grammar are synthetic. The score measures agreement with the simulator's canonical route, so alternative routes to the same goal can receive a zero. The paper trained models on data from the benchmark, while the chat prompt describes the simulator's movement rules. [Original study, Sections 4–6](https://datasets-benchmarks-proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2021/file/2838023a778dfaecdc212708f721b788-Paper-round1.pdf), [Simulator](https://github.com/frankaging/Reason-SCAN/blob/1e6726aab70c915a3d3068bed77ae255feeaf6f1/code/dataset/world.py)
